text: As the Patriots prepare for their Week 3 trip to Jacksonville, the team is leaning on some innovative preparation methods—including a new "mobile classroom" at the New Balance Athletics Center—while grappling with familiar second-half management issues that have plagued them through two games, particularly their clock management decisions late in the second quarter. The defensive scheme looms large for this matchup, with Patriots coordinators drilling down on how to build off successful "X" plays while solving the Jaguars' Cover-6 looks, a coverage the Jacksonville defense is almost certain to deploy; meanwhile, the Jacksonville offense under Trevor Lawrence will be hungry to bounce back from their worst performance in eleven months and capitalize on a Patriots team that by their own admission is still "finding ourselves." On the injury front, there's encouraging news with rookie tight end Eli Raridon returning to practice, though his status remains monitored ahead of Sunday, while the organization took time this week to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with cornerback Christian Gonzalez, tackle Andy Borregales, and teammates at the IBA's new arts center in Boston alongside the Patriots Foundation and Bank of America. Expert predictions are rolling in on the pivotal divisional battle, as both teams look to establish themselves early in what's shaping up to be a crucial AFC East contest.
